title: EFX from a Singleton-Bundle Sufficient Condition
body_html:
EFX from a Singleton-Bundle Sufficient Condition

Lemma. If every bundle in an allocation $A$ has cardinality $\le 1$ (at most one item per agent), then $A$ is automatically EFX ([[social_choice.fair_division.indivisible.efx]]).

In Lean: SocialChoice.FairDivision.Indivisible.isEFX_of_singleton_bundle.
proof_html:
sketch

For agents $i \ne j$ and $g \in A(j)$, since $|A(j)| \le 1$ the bundle equality $A(j) = \{g\}$ holds. Removing $g$ gives $A(j) \setminus \{g\} = \emptyset$, and the EFX inequality becomes $v_i(\emptyset) \le v_i(A(i))$.

For valuations satisfying the natural nonnegativity convention $v_i(\emptyset) \le v_i(S)$ for every $S$ — including additive valuations with nonnegative weights or any monotone valuation — this holds for free. The actual lemma in Lean takes the relevant nonnegativity hypothesis as a parameter to keep the abstract Valuation API uncommitted to monotonicity.

Significance

This is the base case for several EFX existence proofs:

  • For 2 agents and 2 goods, an EFX allocation exists by giving each agent one item (each bundle is a singleton, so the lemma applies directly). See [[social_choice.fair_division.indivisible.efx_two_agents_two_goods]].

  • For a finer item enumeration (giving items one-by-one to the agent with strictly fewer items so far), the resulting allocation has bundles of size at most one when $|G| \le n$ — every agent gets a singleton or empty bundle, again triggering this lemma.

References

  • [AGT Chapter 11] Nisan, Roughgarden, Tardos, and Vazirani, Algorithmic Game Theory, references/AlgorithmicGameTheory.pdf. EFX special cases.
